declarations.name: AppBarElement
declarations.description: A Material Design app bar component.
declarations.summary: A Material Design app bar component.

attributes.name: centered
attributes.description: Whether the title and subtitle are centered instead of leading-aligned (the M3 Expressive "centered text" configuration). Defaults to `false`.

attributes.name: scroll-behavior
attributes.description: How the app bar reacts to scrolling: `hide` (hide on scroll down, reveal on scroll up) or `compress` (medium and large flexible app bars become small until scrolled back to the top).

attributes.name: scrolled
attributes.description: Whether the app bar is in its scrolled state. Defaults to `false`. A medium or large flexible app bar in its scrolled state is shown as a small one (app-bars.md: "When scrolled, medium flexible and large flexible app bars can transform into small app bars").

attributes.name: scroll-target
attributes.description: The id of the element whose scrolling drives `scroll-behavior`. Defaults to the window.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: The size of the app bar (`sm`, `md`, `lg`). Defaults to `sm`.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: The behavioral variant of the app bar (`standard` or `search`). Defaults to `standard`.

attributes.name: density
attributes.description: The density of the buttons inside, from 0 (default) to -3. Each step down removes 4px from the buttons' height (button-groups.md: "Button groups adapt to the height of the buttons inside, including when density is applied"); touch targets stay 48px. A button's own non-zero `density` wins. Values are clamped to that range.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Whether the button group is disabled.

attributes.name: overflow-menu
attributes.description: Whether the buttons at the trailing edge that do not fit collapse into a trailing overflow menu, and come back when the group has room again (button-groups.md, Adaptive design: "Buttons at the trailing edge of the button group can be customized to collapse into an overflow menu at smaller breakpoints, and become visible again at larger sizes."). The group is as wide as its container allows: give it a width, or put it in a narrower container, to make buttons overflow. Choosing a menu entry clicks the original button.

attributes.name: required
attributes.description: Whether selection is required in single-select mode.

attributes.name: resizing
attributes.description: How the group and its buttons resize (button-groups.md, Resizing). `fixed`: every button keeps the width its own size and width give it. `flexible`: the group fills the width of its container and its buttons grow with it; an icon button does not stretch past its set width, and a button with `resizing="fixed"` keeps its width. A button with `resizing="flexible"` in a fixed group grows when the group is given more width. Unset: a connected group is flexible (it spans its surface), a standard group is fixed.

slots.description: Shown in the primary pane of a two-pane list-detail layout while `detail-open` is false (no item selected). Levitate (spec: scaffold, "Levitate"): with `levitate="floating"` or `levitate="docked"`, the secondary pane of a supporting pane or feed layout floats above the primary pane (or docks to the bottom edge at compact, like a bottom sheet) in windows too small for two co-planar panes, while `levitate-open` is set. `levitate-modal` makes it modal: a scrim covers the panes, the primary pane is inert, focus moves into the pane and back to the trigger, and the pane closes when something behind it is used or Escape is pressed. Modality is scoped to the scaffold; use `md-gb-dialog` or `md-gb-sheet` for app-wide modals. At large and extra-large windows a levitated pane keeps floating (spec: "On large screens, floating panes are the default"); the scrim is optional (`levitate-modal` adds it). `levitate-coplanar` opts into a co-planar pane there instead. `levitate-draggable` and `levitate-resizable` add a move handle and a resize corner to a floating pane: drag them, or focus them and use the arrow keys (Shift moves in larger steps). `levitate-change` fires after each move or resize. Foldables: the scaffold reads the fold (hinge) from the Viewport Segments API and keeps panes off it. A vertical fold splits two panes at the fold with the spacer on it (at least the spacer width); a horizontal fold (tabletop) stacks the supporting pane below it. The fold crossing the scaffold is reflected as the `fold` attribute (`vertical` or `horizontal`). Browsers without the API keep the regular layout.

declarations.description: A Material Design gBreeze toolbar custom element.
declarations.summary: A Material Design gBreeze toolbar custom element.

attributes.name: color
attributes.description: The color scheme of the toolbar.

attributes.name: docked
attributes.description: Whether the toolbar is docked across full width.

attributes.name: expanded
attributes.description: Whether a floating toolbar with a FAB shows its items. When `false`, the toolbar collapses and its FAB grows to the medium size (Compose floating toolbar `expanded`). Set `expanded="false"` from markup.

attributes.name: fab-position
attributes.description: Which side of a floating toolbar the FAB is on (`end` or `start`).

attributes.name: orientation
attributes.description: The layout orientation.

attributes.name: overflow-menu
attributes.description: Whether trailing actions that do not fit move into an overflow menu in the trailing slot (toolbars.md, Adaptive design). On by itself when an `overflow` slot trigger is provided; this turns it on with the default "More actions" button.

attributes.name: scroll-behavior
attributes.description: How a docked or floating toolbar reacts to scrolling: `hide` slides it beyond the bottom edge when the page scrolls down and back on scroll up (toolbars.md: docked and floating toolbars "can animate offscreen").

attributes.name: scroll-target
attributes.description: The id of the element whose scrolling drives `scroll-behavior`. Defaults to the window.

declarations.name: TooltipElement
declarations.description: A Material Design plain or rich tooltip.
declarations.summary: A Material Design plain or rich tooltip.

attributes.name: align
attributes.description: How the tooltip lines up with its anchor along the placement side: `center` (plain default) or `start` (rich default). A rich tooltip can be `center`ed below its anchor on desktop.

attributes.name: caret
attributes.description: Whether to draw a caret pointing at the anchor.

attributes.name: hide-delay
attributes.description: Delay before hiding after the pointer leaves, in milliseconds.

attributes.name: for
attributes.description: The id of the anchor element, in the same root as the tooltip.

attributes.name: no-boundary
attributes.description: Plain only: the anchor has no visual boundary, such as a text baseline, so the tooltip sits 8dp from it instead of 4dp.

attributes.name: open
attributes.description: Whether the tooltip is open.

attributes.name: persistent
attributes.description: Rich only: opens when the anchor is clicked instead of on hover / focus, and stays open until the user interacts with another element.

attributes.name: placement
attributes.description: Preferred side of the anchor. Defaults to `above` for plain tooltips and `below` for rich ones. Flips when there isn't room.

attributes.name: quick
attributes.description: Skips the open / close animation.

attributes.name: show-delay
attributes.description: Hover delay before showing, in milliseconds.

attributes.name: subhead
attributes.description: Rich only: subhead text. Replaced by content in the `subhead` slot.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: Plain or rich.
